For those using Easy Electrophysiology in published research, our RRID is [RRID:SCR_021190](https://scicrunch.org/resolver/RRID:SCR_021190).

## Neo

Easy Electrophysiology uses Neo [@garcia2014], a data-loading package that handles many electrophysiological filetypes.

We also thank the contributing authors of the relevant Neo submodules including Forrest Collman, Harald Hentschke (Axon files) and Jeffrey Gill (AxoGraph files).

## Events Template Matching

The template matching event detection algorithm with a biexponential template and correlation coefficient threshold was first described by @jonas1993.

The Detection Criterion thresholding method was introduced by @clements1997.

The deconvolution method for template event detection was introduced by @pernia2012.

## Action potential threshold detection

Easy Electrophysiology provides a number of options for threshold estimation in *Action Potential Kinetics* analysis, including Method I and II from @sekerli2004 and maximum curvature threshold detection from @rossokhin1992.

## Spike Frequency Accommodation -- Local Variance

The Local Variance measure for spike frequency accommodation is from @shinomoto2003.

## LogISI

The logISI method was introduced and extensively detailed by @pasquale2010.

## PyQtGraph

We would also like to thank Luke Campagnola and the PyQtGraph team for their work on the excellent [PyQtGraph package](https://www.pyqtgraph.org) that provides high performance, flexible graphing.
